Time zone rule revision exposure measures the UTC hours for which old and new offsets disagree within a window. Use it when an agent needs the duration and maximum size of an edition discrepancy.

Calendar date migration identifies whether the same UTC instant changes its local reporting date or weekday between editions. Use it when an agent needs the accounting date of a timestamp near local m
Local event migration returns all UTC candidates for a wall clock under the old and new time zone data. Use it when an agent needs the actual instants affected by a gap, fold or offset revision.
Time zone database comparison returns old and new local displays for one UTC instant under two IANA releases. Use it when an agent needs the wall time change after a tzdata upgrade.
Historical station availability separates hours missing at one rain gauge from simultaneous data gaps. Use it when an agent needs a decision on pairing two archived records.
Historical dry-window search counts uninterrupted intervals dry at both sites for a minimum number of hours. Use it when an agent needs a two-site outdoor work window.
Historical rainfall reports Pearson correlation of paired hourly depths, including observed dry hours. Use it when an agent needs the strength of synchronized intensity changes.
Historical rainfall finds the largest absolute running depth difference between two stations over matched hours. Use it when an agent needs the point of maximum accumulated divergence.
Historical precipitation comparison counts simultaneous readings within a chosen millimetre tolerance. Use it when an agent needs gauge agreement under a stated tolerance.
Historical rainfall identifies the longest run when the first station reported rain and the other stayed dry. Use it when an agent needs a localized precipitation interval.
Historical rain intensity locates the hour with the highest combined depth while both stations recorded rain. Use it when an agent needs a jointly observed intensity peak.
Historical rainfall timing finds the hour shift with the greatest wet-hour intersection over union. Use it when an agent needs an observed offset between station records.
Historical rain overlap measures how often the second station was wet when the first station was wet. Use it when an agent needs a conditional wet-hour frequency.
Historical rainfall compares accumulated depth at two German stations using only jointly observed hours. Use it when an agent needs a like-for-like precipitation difference.

Soil temperature threshold disagreement counts complete dates on which the 5 and 50 cm daily means fall on opposite sides of a cutoff. Use it when an agent needs days when shallow and deep sensors imp

Soil temperature depth-weighted temperature integrates the observed profile from 5 to 50 cm assuming linear change between adjacent sensors. Use it when an agent needs a mean for the measured soil lay

Soil temperature freeze and thaw transitions count sign changes in consecutive daily means at the specified sensor depth. Use it when an agent needs freeze-thaw transitions without bridging missing da
Soil temperature inversion frequency counts days on which all four daily means strictly increase with depth. Use it when an agent needs the frequency of a fully inverted soil profile.
Soil temperature peak timing compares the first shallow and deep maxima and their signed calendar-day lag. Use it when an agent needs the timing difference between two soil layers.
Soil temperature degree days integrate positive daily mean temperatures above a chosen base at one sampled depth. Use it when an agent needs a thermal accumulation for the selected station.
Soil temperature buffering compares the observed ranges at 5 and 50 cm on the same dates. Use it when an agent needs the fraction of surface variability transmitted to the deeper layer.
Soil temperature frost penetration reports the deepest sampled layer with a below-zero daily mean and the first matching date. Use it when an agent needs evidence of subsurface frost in daily means.
Soil temperature gradient identifies the strongest absolute 5-to-50 cm temperature gradient with its sign. Use it when an agent needs the steepest observed shallow-to-deep change.
Soil temperature profile returns the newest complete observed 5, 10, 20 and 50 cm thermal profile in the selected window. Use it when an agent needs a dated measurement at each depth.
Historical wind gust separation finds the largest absolute difference between daily peak gust and mean wind speed. Use it when an agent needs wind variability in metres per second.
Historical wind gust comparison counts same-date threshold exceedances at two weather stations. Use it when an agent needs joint exposure across two locations.
Historical wind gust coverage identifies missing calendar days within a requested station interval. Use it when an agent needs sampling gaps before comparing extreme weather.
Historical wind gust exceedance intensity sums the positive differences between daily maxima and a speed threshold. Use it when an agent needs the magnitude of gusty days above a chosen level.
Historical wind gust quantiles return the median and 90th percentile of daily peak speeds using linear interpolation. Use it when an agent needs the distribution of daily gusts.
Historical wind gust changes report the largest signed increase across adjacent observation dates. Use it when an agent needs the sharpest daily change.
Historical wind gust factors identify the day with the largest peak divided by same-day mean wind speed. Use it when an agent needs the strongest relative gustiness.
Historical wind gust runs find the longest sequence of adjacent observed days meeting a speed threshold. Use it when an agent needs the duration of a windy spell.
Historical wind gust frequency counts observed days at or above a given peak speed. Use it when an agent needs a historical threshold frequency.
Historical wind gust extremes return the first peak date and the daily peak in metres per second and kilometres per hour. Use it when an agent needs the observed strongest gust in a window.
Historical snow depth interruptions identify observed bare-ground runs bounded by snow on both sides. Use it when an agent needs mid-period breaks in snow cover.
Historical snow depth quantiles return nearest-rank quartiles and median over measured days, including zeros. Use it when an agent needs the distribution of daily snowpack.
Historical snow depth completeness reports absent measurement days and the longest gap in the request. Use it when an agent needs evidence of observation gaps.
Historical snow depth transitions count observed upward and downward crossings of a specified depth. Use it when an agent needs repeat crossings during a period.
Historical snow depth decline finds the largest depth loss between consecutive observed days. Use it when an agent needs the largest measured snowpack reduction.
Historical snow depth accumulation finds the largest positive depth change between consecutive measured days. Use it when an agent needs the largest observed buildup.
Historical snow depth exposure sums observed daily depths into centimetre-days and reports missing days. Use it when an agent needs integrated snowpack exposure.
Historical snow depth spells return the longest uninterrupted observed run meeting a minimum depth. Use it when an agent needs continuous snow cover.
Historical snow depth coverage returns the number and percentage of observed days meeting a depth threshold. Use it when an agent needs the frequency of sufficient cover.
Historical snow depth peaks return the maximum measured snow depth and the first and last dates at that maximum. Use it when an agent needs a dated snowpack maximum.
US historical AQI rolling means identify the seven consecutive observed days with the highest mean daily index. Use it when an agent needs the highest sustained seven-day average.
US AQI completeness returns reported days, unreported days and the longest missing calendar span. Use it when an agent needs to qualify a county time series.
US air quality episodes return the longest consecutive observed run at or above an AQI threshold. Use it when an agent needs persistent high-index periods.
US historical AQI peaks return the maximum daily index and its first and last occurrences. Use it when an agent needs extreme reported days.
US historical air quality returns the reported daily AQI, defining pollutant and site count for a county. Use it when an agent needs an EPA daily observation.
Historical saturation proximity returns the smallest observed temperature minus estimated dew point. Use it when an agent needs the hour closest to saturation.
